newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia bln-dlr bond to clear energy debt.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia bln-dlr bond to clear energy debt.

text.p: Russia will launch billion-dollar domestic bond programmes in August to clear staggering unpaid debts owed to and by the federal government, a senior fuel and energy ministry official said on Thursday.

First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko said the federal government and energy companies which are tangled in a multi-billion dollar payments crises would balance out their debts and credits in August. "Bonds will be issued on the difference," he said.
The government, which is the larger debtor, will issue the bonds, Kiriyenko told reporters. "This is a revolution," he added. "The government is saying 'I will pay my debts'."

"The first tranches will appear in August," he said. He declined to name a hard figure for the issue. "Realistically we can talk about 3-5 trillion roubles ($520-$860 million) -- more than that requires further work."
The bonds are expected to have a 3-7 year maturity and a projected hard currency yield of 4.5 percent, he said.

Separately the Finance Ministry, or regional governments backed by the ministry, will issue about three trillion roubles of winter energy bonds with projected one-year maturities beginning about August 15 to securitise regional debts to the federal government for previous years' winter supplies.
Russia is increasingly trying to clean up its books and raise funds by converting old debts into tradeable securities, creating a stronger domestic bond market in the process.

First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov told a cabinet meeting Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdan had signed an order on the winter energy bonds and an order requiring ministries to limit their energy use.
That will allow the federal government to pay its current bills and pay its past debts with bonds.

The Finance Ministry in June began a programme for regions to issue about nine trillion roubles of farm bonds to repay 1996 agricultural credits from the federal government. Kiriyenko said the winter energy bond programme would be similar.
Russia's largest company, national electric utility Unified Energy System, will issue another $1 billion in bonds convertible into company shares.
Kiriyenko said all the proceeds would go to the government as privatisation revenues or to pay debts and company officials say the programme will launch in the fall.

The regional winter energy bonds for unpaid winter supplies will probably be sold for cash that will be handed to the federal government to clear the regions' debts to Moscow. The government's own paper restructured from debt to energy companies would be given directly to the companies, which could hold or trade them, officials have said. ($ = 5,793 roubles)
